summary: Completed one bounded, fresh technical-feasibility review of docs/live-deployment-plan.md (SHA-256 43314dff16873432163a1a371350c1d3c1d618857caefb8a04b0c7785d9ba949). No supported technical errors were identified within the assigned scope. The architecture is a feasible candidate subject to the plan's explicit provider, recovery, identity, capacity, and admission gates; this is not a hosted-readiness result.
coverage: Read the complete plan, lines 1-218. Confirmed its digest matches the assignment. Read the project startup context, workflow, adversarial-review contract/schema, and docs-writer guidance. Review used fresh task context.

Cloud Run timers, port, image platform, and shutdown: examined apps/server/src/startup.ts matches, apps/server/src/server.ts, apps/server/src/index.ts matches, scheduler/ticker matches, and Dockerfile. Source supports VISUA_PORT rather than generic PORT, explicit host binding, timer-driven work, and bounded shutdown. Provider documentation supports instance-based CPU plus minimum instances, linux/amd64, and the ten-second termination interval: https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/billing-settings ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/container-contract . No runtime timing was measured.

Cloud SQL connection/session semantics: examined apps/server/src/storage/postgres.ts, apps/server/src/storage/events.ts listener implementation, and apps/server/src/operations/pilot-preflight.ts. Confirmed the default ten-connection pool plus separate LISTEN client and the preflight's URL-host/database syntax constraints. The plan correctly leaves an exact-image socket/proxy/TLS connection proof open: https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/connect-run .

Workspace identity choice: inspected auth configuration and service matches for discovery, openid/email/profile scopes, email_verified, and issuer/subject linking. Cross-checked Internal audience organizational eligibility and the distinction between the hd hint and verified hd claim: https://developers.google.com/workspace/guides/configure-oauth-consent ; https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/15549945 ; https://developers.google.com/identity/openid-connect/reference .

Cloudflare DNS and ingress: inspected the plan's DNS-only initial path, preservation of Workspace records, load-balancer custom domain, origin certificate, and later proxy acceptance requirements. Provider documentation supports the recommended external Application Load Balancer path and Full (strict) certificate requirements: https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/mapping-custom-domains ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/ssl-modes/full-strict/ .

R2 compatibility and recovery: examined apps/server/src/blobs/s3.ts and blobs/index.ts, including explicit ChecksumSHA256 on PutObject and configurable endpoint/path style. Verified bucket-scoped credentials, account endpoint/auto region, and unsupported PutBucketVersioning in provider documentation: https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/get-started/s3/ ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/api/s3/api/ . The plan appropriately requires exact-SDK upload/read/cleanup proof and independently retained artifact copies before selecting R2.

Scale, cost, rollback, and setup gates: reviewed lines 16-30, 86-107, 149-218 for separate environments, project/billing setup, named pending inputs, connection budget with rollout overlap, pre-creation estimate, stopped writers, coordinated backups, restore to fresh destinations, previous compatible image, and explicit reconciliation of later writes. These are proposed acceptance conditions, not measurements.
limitations: Read-only plan/source/provider-documentation review only. No builds, application tests, security exploit reproduction, cloud account access, credential reads, provisioning, or live service operations were performed.

All feasibility conclusions are source/documentation-derived predictions. No Google login, Cloud SQL connection, Cloud Run timer/shutdown behavior, R2 operation, restore, capacity, or alert delivery was measured.

R2's current checksum compatibility table distinguishes full-object and composite SHA-256 support. Documentation alone does not establish whether Visua's exact single PutObject request and installed AWS SDK succeed; the plan's explicit R2 compatibility gate remains mandatory.

The exact Cloud SQL connection string and authentication method remain unselected. A socket/proxy configuration must satisfy both node-postgres and preflight URL parsing while preserving a dedicated LISTEN session; the plan explicitly defers this proof.
Domain names, organization/project identifiers, region/residency, users/workload, budget, recovery objectives, and accountable operators are pending. No cost or capacity figure is established.

The brief declared HEAD cb438d1; no git commands were run under the assignment's restrictions. The reviewed plan bytes were independently hash-checked. No application-security review or disposition of the referenced F01/F02/F03 findings is included.
